notes.12: Question 12 incorrectly as they chose B ( des devoirs à faire ) rather than A ( un moment de libre ). Christophe states that he has already finished his homework and now has some free time. Exercise 4 Question 16 For this piece of writing, there are 3 marks available for the communication of three pieces of information, indicated by illustrations, and 2 marks for accurate use of language. Candidates were asked to write an email to a friend, saying: Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French (Foreign Language) June 2014 (a) what time it is (Il est neuf/9 heures). (b) where the candidate is in the house ( Je suis dans le salon/la salle de séjour ). (c) what the candidate is doing ( J’écoute de la musique ). This exercise was generally well handled with many candidates scoring full marks for communication and at least 1 mark for language. The naming of the room proved to be the most demanding task as the French for lounge/living room/television room was not well known. La salle on its own was not rewarded but it was when followed by de télévision or de famille. In order to score the 2 marks available for appropriateness of language, candidates had to use two correct verbs in appropriate tenses. Where candidates did not score full marks for language this was usually on account of using C’est… rather than Il est … in task (a) . Candidates should be aware that credit is only given for the required tasks, which can be completed briefly, as in the examples above. Some candidates wrote overlong responses to the task and sometimes ignored the specific information required. Irrelevant material, no matter how well expressed, is not rewarded and candidates could make better use of their time on other exercises. Section 2 Exercise 1 Questions 17-24 For this exercise, candidates were asked to read a longer piece of text (an email from Patrick in which he describes his holiday adventures) and answer questions in French. The focus of this exercise is to test candidates’ ability to locate the correct answer to each question in the text provided. Therefore, although often a one or two word answer was sufficient, provided that what the candidate had written contained the correct information, answers lifted directly from the text were acceptable, even if they contained a lot of extra material. This additional material was ignored except in the few instances where it contradicted the correct answer. The majority of candidates coped well, and scored equally well. For Question 17 the expected answer was dans un centre de loisirs or près de Biarritz, for Question 18 , les lits sont trop durs. For Question 19 , the correct answer was passer tout le temps en plein air and not il est très sportif. Question 20 was very successfully answered and most located the correct piece of information – la planche à voile. Some lost the mark for Question 21 as they answered il n’a pas réussi à rester debout rather than the expected il tombait (tout le temps). Question 22 required three pieces of information: plus petit, plus facile à contrôler and il n’y a pas de voile. Most candidates scored the 3 marks available. Some lost a mark by stating c’est mieux without any reference to planche à voile . Question 23 and Question 24 were very well answered. Exercise 2 Question 25 This writing task – a short essay of 80 to 90 words – was well within the experience of all candidates. Candidates were required to: (a) Describe a member of their family. (b) Explain why they like him/her. (c) Say what they intend to do with that person next weekend and why. The vast majority of candidates scored the 10 marks available for communication as they found plenty to say about their chosen person. They provided many details about physical appearance, character, job, leisure activities. Reasons for liking the person often included the help and support the candidates received from them, the presents they were bought and what they did together or had in common. Activities they would do together the following weekend often included going to the cinema or a restaurant, playing a sport together or going shopping. The vast majority of candidates scored 5 or 4 of the 5 marks available for language. There was some confusion as to the use of il/elle est… or il/elle a... The spelling of cheveux was not always well known and some used chevaux instead. Candidates used a wide variety of adjectives when describing personality. The last task expected them to say what they would do next weekend. Some candidates were not secure in their use of the future tense or je voudrais plus an infinitive. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French (Foreign Language) June 2014 Section 3 In Section 3 , candidates are expected to show a more precise level of understanding of longer French texts. It is no longer enough just to be able to locate the correct area of the text which will supply the answer looked for. Candidates need to show that they have understood the text and have focused on precisely the details required for the answer. While it will be possible to lift some answers from the text, candidates need to be very discriminating in what they choose – additional material copied may invalidate an otherwise correct answer. Exercise 1 Questions 26-31 In this exercise, having read the text, candidates have to make up their minds which of the given statements are Vrai and which are Faux (they are told two are Vrai and four are Faux) . Having made their choice, they must then go on to correct the false statements in the style of the example given. There is no credit given for a version which just adds ... ne...pas... to the original statement (or vice versa). Where candidates decide that an answer is Vrai , the box must be ticked or no mark can be scored. Questions 26, 27 and 30 were the three most often incorrectly identified as true or false. The others were usually correctly ticked. For Question 26 , which was Faux , candidates could select from the text that elle mettait des vêtements que sa mère avait portés. The addition of ou alors invalidated the answer. Question 27 was Vrai and required no correction. The correction for Question 28 ( elle demandait aux gens qu’elle trouvait bien habillés si elle pouvait les photographier) was usually well done. To score the mark for Question 29 , candidates needed to state that des companies financent son blog or that les companies paient Clémence pour faire de la publicité sur son blog. Many candidates successfully stated il suffit d’avoir un peu d’imagination to correct
notes.30: Question 30 . Question 31 was the second Vrai statement. Exercise 2 Questions 32-39 This final comprehension exercise was, as intended, the most demanding part of the paper and many candidates found it quite challenging. Most could clearly access the general meaning of the text and generally understood the questions. Many were able to locate the correct part of the text relevant to the question but they were often not selective enough in formulating an answer. Some were unable to manipulate their answer sufficiently to give an acceptable response. In this exercise, candidates need to be able to make the necessary changes between direct and reported speech and to deal with the resulting pronoun / possessive adjective confusion.
notes.32: Question 32 was usually well done by candidates who succinctly answered tous les jeudis . Candidates who chose to use the finite verb passe were expected to include a subject before it, either elle… or l’émission passe… . Question 33 was well answered as candidates successfully located «Un pays là-bas» vient d’obtenir le prix de la meilleure émission de l’année . Question 34 was in two parts. For (a) des/les paysages was sufficient to score the mark. For (b), many did not score the mark, as they lifted l’essentiel est de les laisser parler without identifying to whom les referred. The expected answer was laisser parler les gens . Question 35 was also in two parts and was usually well done as candidates correctly answered (a ) les voyages organisés and (b) il trouve ça vraiment triste de ne jamais rencontrer les habitants . Candidates sometimes found it difficult to manipulate the language required to answer Question 36 and often offered je voulais absolument montrer à mes auditeurs que ces gens étaient comme eux. To be acceptable the sentence had to be put in the third person singular – il voulait (absolument) montrer à ses auditeurs que ces gens étaient comme eux . Question 37 was relatively straightforward and many candidates were able to offer an acceptable answer – il a pris la décision de passer/il a passé (plus d’) un mois dans une famille indienne. Question 38 and Question 39 were extremely well answered. Cambridge International General Certificate of Secondary Education 0520 French (Foreign Language) June 2014 FRENCH (Foreign Language)
